result.topic_en: This two-page spread (pp. 262–263) gives the rule for when 10^p ∓ 1 is divisible by a prime 2p+1, then a general theorem on when a^p − 1 or a^p + 1 is divisible by 2p+1 for primes of the form 4an ∓ (2f+1), with two corollaries. It then states the problem of deciding which of a^p ∓ 1 is divisible, solved by quadratic residues, with the start of the proof.

Theorema generale.

§. 32. Quicunque fuerit numerus $a$, si $2p+1$ denotet numerum primum et casu $p=f$ innotuerit, vtrum formula $a^f-1$, an $a^f+1$ diuisibilis sit per $2f+1$; tum generatim eiusdem generis formula, siue $a^p-1$, siue $a^p+1$ diuisibilis erit per $2p+1$, si fuerit $2p+1=4an\mp(2f+1)$, quicunque numerus pro $n$ accipiatur, dummodo inde prodeat $2p+1$ numerus primus.

Corollarium 1.

§. 33. Ex praecedentibus theorematibus satis liquet, casu $f=0$ semper formulam $a^p-1$ diuisibilem fore per $2p+1=4an\mp1$, quoties scilicet hic numerus fuerit primus.

Corollarium 2.

§. 34. Sin autem sit $f=1$, prouti siue $a-1$, siue $a+1$ per 3 diuidi potest, simili casu generatim siue for-

formula $a^p\mp1$ [?] per numerum primum $2p+1$ erit diuisibilis, quoties $2p+1$ in hac forma: $4an\pm3$ continetur.

Scholion.

§. 35. Theoremata autem particularia allata facile vlterius continuari possunt, si sequens problema in subsidium vocetur, cuius quidem solutio firmissimis rationibus innititur.

Problema.

§. 36. Quicunque fuerit numerus $a$, si $2p+1$ denotet numerum primum, quouis casu oblato inuestigare, vtrum formula $a^p-1$, an altera $a^p+1$ diuisibilis sit per $2p+1$.

Solutio.

Quaerantur omnia residua, quae ex diuisione quadratorum per numerum $2p+1$ resultant, quae sint $1$; $\alpha$; $\beta$; $\gamma$; $\delta$; etc. multitudine $=p$, numeri autem ab his diuersi non-residua appellentur. Quo facto si numerus $a$ inter residua reperiatur; tum semper formula $a^p-1$ erit diuisibilis; sin autem numerus $a$ inter non-residua occurrat; tum altera formula $a^p+1$ diuisibilis erit. Haec autem regula ita demonstratur: Si fuerit $a$ residuum ex cuiusdam quadrati $x^2$ diuisione per $2p+1$ natum; tum erit $x^2-a$ per $2p+1$ diuisibile; siue aequabitur cuipiam multiplo $m(2p+1)$; ita vt sit $a=x^2-m(2p+1)$. Hinc ergo fiet $a^p=(x^2-m(2p+1))^p$, quae potestas per $2p+1$ diuisa idem residuum relinquet ac potestas

items.quote: Quicunque fuerit numerus $a$, si $2p+1$ denotet numerum primum et casu $p=f$ innotuerit, vtrum formula $a^f-1$, an $a^f+1$ diuisibilis sit per $2f+1$; tum generatim eiusdem generis formula, siue $a^p-1$, siue $a^p+1$ diuisibilis erit per $2p+1$, si fuerit $2p+1=4an\mp(2f+1)$, quicunque numerus pro $n$ accipiatur, dummodo inde prodeat $2p+1$ numerus primus.
items.english: Whatever the number a, if 2p+1 denotes a prime and it is known for the case p=f whether a^f − 1 or a^f + 1 is divisible by 2f+1, then in general the formula of the same kind, either a^p − 1 or a^p + 1, will be divisible by 2p+1 whenever 2p+1 = 4an ∓ (2f+1), for any n, provided 2p+1 comes out prime.

items.quote: casu $f=0$ semper formulam $a^p-1$ diuisibilem fore per $2p+1=4an\mp1$, quoties scilicet hic numerus fuerit primus.
items.english: In the case f=0, the formula a^p − 1 will always be divisible by 2p+1 = 4an ∓ 1, whenever that number is prime.

items.quote: Sin autem sit $f=1$, prouti siue $a-1$, siue $a+1$ per 3 diuidi potest, simili casu generatim siue formula $a^p\mp1$ [?] per numerum primum $2p+1$ erit diuisibilis, quoties $2p+1$ in hac forma: $4an\pm3$ continetur.
items.english: If f=1, then according as a − 1 or a + 1 is divisible by 3, correspondingly in general the formula a^p ∓ 1 will be divisible by the prime 2p+1, whenever 2p+1 is of the form 4an ± 3.

items.quote: Quicunque fuerit numerus $a$, si $2p+1$ denotet numerum primum, quouis casu oblato inuestigare, vtrum formula $a^p-1$, an altera $a^p+1$ diuisibilis sit per $2p+1$.
items.english: Whatever the number a, if 2p+1 denotes a prime, to determine in any given case whether the formula a^p − 1 or the other one, a^p + 1, is divisible by 2p+1.

items.quote: si numerus $a$ inter residua reperiatur; tum semper formula $a^p-1$ erit diuisibilis; sin autem numerus $a$ inter non-residua occurrat; tum altera formula $a^p+1$ diuisibilis erit.
items.english: If the number a is found among the residues, then the formula a^p − 1 will always be divisible; but if a occurs among the non-residues, then the other formula a^p + 1 will be divisible.
